[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Handling Late-Arriving Dimensions and Facts in ETL"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In modern data warehousing, data rarely arrives in the exact order it was generated. Network latency, batch processing failures, and distributed source systems often cause records to arrive out of sequence. Designing robust ETL pipelines to handle late-arriving dimensions and facts is critical for maintaining reporting accuracy."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Late-Arriving Dimensions"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A late-arriving dimension occurs when a fact table record arrives and references a dimension key that does not yet exist in the dimension table. For example, a sales transaction for a new store arrives before the store profile has been loaded into theDim_Store table."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Strategies for Late-Arriving Dimensions"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dummy or Placeholder Records: Insert a default record like 'Unknown' or 'Pending' with a predefined surrogate key (e.g., -1) to satisfy foreign key constraints."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Inference: If partial information is known from the fact record, insert a minimal dimension record with inferred attributes, updating them later when the full dimension batch arrives."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Late-Arriving Facts"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Late-arriving facts occur when historical measurements (such as a transaction from three days ago) are processed after subsequent data has already been loaded. This impacts aggregate reporting, rolling averages, and historical trends."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Solutions via SQL ETL"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following SQL pattern demonstrates how to handle a late-arriving dimension by inserting a placeholder record before loading the fact table."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"INSERT INTO Dim_Customer (customer_id, customer_name, status)
SELECT DISTINCT f.customer_id, 'Pending Registration', 'Inferred'
FROM Staging_Sales f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM Dim_Customer d WHERE d.customer_id = f.customer_id
);"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"By ensuring the dimension key exists prior to the fact table load, you prevent referential integrity violations and ensure reporting consistency across your data warehouse."}]
